definitions.explanation: Whether something is right or wrong, good or bad. Used when evaluating or debating the correctness of an action or policy.

examples.english: To question the right and wrong of something.

examples.japanese: {是非|ぜひ}を{判断|はんだん}するのは{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: It is difficult to judge right from wrong.

examples.japanese: この{政策|せいさく}の{是非|ぜひ}について{議論|ぎろん}された。
examples.english: The merits of this policy were debated.

examples.japanese: {死刑|しけい}{制度|せいど}の{是非|ぜひ}をめぐって{意見|いけん}が{分|わ}かれている。
examples.english: Opinions are divided over the right and wrong of the death penalty system.

notes:
{是非|ぜひ} as a noun means "right and wrong" or "merits and demerits."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {是非|ぜひ}を{問|と}う (to question the rightness of)
- {是非|ぜひ}を{判断|はんだん}する (to judge right and wrong)
- {是非|ぜひ}をめぐって (regarding the merits of)

USAGE:
- This is the noun usage. The adverb {是非|ぜひ} (by all means, definitely) is a separate word with a different function.
- {是|ぜ} means "right/correct" and {非|ひ} means "wrong/incorrect"
